children: Indian shares opened higher on Friday after four consecutive sessions of losses, as fading prospects of a U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike later this month lifted global equities and weighed on bond yields.

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said on Thursday he would support keeping interest rates unchanged at the U.S. central bank's next policy meeting if upcoming data confirms inflation pressures are easing.
Expectations for a rate increase at the Fed's mid-September meeting came down to roughly 50%, versus about 63% in the prior session, according to CME FedWatch.
was up 0.23% at 23,927.1 and the BSE Sensex
added 0.66% to 76,652.19, as of 9:17 a.m. IST.

The Nifty 50 and Sensex fell 1.3% and 1.4%, respectively, during the previous four sessions as higher crude oil prices and bond yields weighed on sentiment.
